clue.text: Yearning after net returns may be seductive

indicators.note: after places the yearning piece behind the turned-round net
returns asks for the word for a net to come back the other way, read from right to left

parts.note: a web is a net, as a spider's
yearning or longing to do something is itching

explanation.surface: Someone whose longing follows a net coming back might be alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the net word and 'after' puts the yearning word behind it; 'may be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bewitching casts a spell, so it is enchanting and seductive.

clue.text: Money's not right for singer

indicators.note: not tells us the right abbreviation must be absent from the money word

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A performer is told that cash is not the right reason to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is northern English slang for money; 'not' removes R to leave BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male singer with the lowest voice range.

clue.text: Something or other employing old serving women in religious festival

indicators.note: in places the servicewomen's abbreviation within the festival name

parts.note: Whit, or Whitsun, is the Christian festival of Pentecost
the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army in WWII

explanation.surface: A vague thing involving elderly waitresses at a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'serving women' are not waitresses but servicewomen: the ATS was Britain's wartime women's army corps. 'employing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit is a vague word for any thing whose name escapes you, a thingummy.

clue.text: In circuit, that man has to finish broadcasting detective story

indicators.note: In puts the man and the broadcasting phrase within the word for a circuit

parts.note: a tour is a circuit, a round trip
he means that man
to sign off is to end a broadcast

explanation.surface: On a tour, a presenter must wrap up a crime programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' wraps the circuit round the rest. The answer is a Sherlock Holmes novel by Arthur Conan Doyle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the second Sherlock Holmes novel, a classic piece of detective fiction.

clue.text: Dashing to look at unfinished area of North London

parts.note: haring means running fast, dashing like a hare

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the looking word is dropped

parts.note: to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Rushing to glance at part of a city before getting to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts EYE to EY. HARINGEY is a London borough in the north of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Haringey is a borough in the north of London, so an area of that part of the city.

clue.text: May gets upset by endless hot Mexican food

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word for may is written bottom to top

parts.note: may and can both express being allowed

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the heat word

parts.note: the word hot is used for its own letters

explanation.surface: A woman named May is disappointed by a constant spicy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like a name or month; it is the verb, CAN, which 'upset' turns to NAC. 'endless' cuts HOT to HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip topped with cheese, a Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: Man hugging wife was dizzy

indicators.note: hugging means the man's name wraps around the abbreviation for wife

parts.note: Sam is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man embracing his wife felt light-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: Any man's name can stand for 'man'; SAM fits round W.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swims you feel giddy, so it swam means it was dizzy.

clue.text: Overlooking one engaged in curling

indicators.note: engaged in means the numeral for one is set inside the curling word

parts.note: waving hair is curling
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone ignoring a person taking part in the sport of curling.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling looks like the ice sport; it is hair curling, WAVING, with I set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiving a rule or fee means setting it aside, so overlooking it.

clue.text: Economic theorist ruined minor state

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An economist wrecked a small country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals an anagram of MINOR STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetarist is an economist who holds that controlling the money supply governs the economy.

clue.text: Fish behind second rock

indicators.note: behind places the fish after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish swims behind another rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like a stone, but it is the verb, as in rock a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock something is to shake it back and forth.

clue.text: No rises unfortunately around European Community — in this?

definitions.text: No rises unfortunately around European Community — in this?

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters round the community abbreviation
unfortunately says the letters of no rises are badly rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lack of growth across Europe means a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged NO RISES goes round EC. The whole clue doubles as the meaning: a period with no rises across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a period of economic decline in which there are no rises in output.

clue.text: Insufficient vote for simple mathematical procedure

parts.note: short means insufficient, lacking
in Parliament a vote is called a division

explanation.surface: Too few votes for an easy maths operation.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament a vote is a division, as members divide into lobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Short division is a basic method of dividing by a single-digit number without written working.

clue.text: Crazy sect is looting member of church

indicators.note: crazy signals the letters of the three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mad cult is plundering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' signals an anagram of SECT IS LOOTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scientologist belongs to the Church of Scientology.

clue.text: Medic rails about refusal to take responsibility

indicators.note: about indicates the letters of the two words are moved around

explanation.surface: A doctor complains noisily about not being blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals an anagram of MEDIC RAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a statement denying liability for something.

clue.text: 'Elpful suggestion stopped fiancé

indicators.note: the apostrophe in this dropped-aitch spelling shows the opening H is lost from the suggestion word

parts.note: a hint is a helpful suggestion
ended means stopped

explanation.surface: A helpful tip ended an engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: ''Elpful' drops its own H, telling you to do the same: HINT loses H to give INT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's intended is the person they plan to marry, their fiancé.

clue.text: An old hand, one putting on a show

definitions.meaning: read literally, a ... is one who stages a production

explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, and one who stages a play is literally a stager.

clue.text: Mining hazard got rid of a politician

parts.note: fired means dismissed, got rid of
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Sacking an MP is risky for miners.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRED + A + MP, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane gas in coal mines, which can explode.

clue.text: See bistro house red primarily and a container for it

indicators.note: house means the bistro word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a café is a bistro

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of red

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A café's house red, served in a jug for the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house red' looks like the wine; 'house' is the verb putting R and A inside CAFE. 'it' is the red wine. 'See' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open glass flask for serving wine at the table.

clue.text: Transport worker runs over wild animal

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the runs abbreviation above the shuffled word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of animal are scrambled

explanation.surface: A railway employee runs over a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like the verb of a car running something over; it is the cricket abbreviation, and 'wild' scrambles the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A railman works on the railways, a transport worker.

clue.text: Is copper being entertained by Scottish football club making a bloomer?

indicators.note: entertained by means the club's name takes the other letters in

parts.note: Hibs is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman entertained by a Scottish club makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman and 'bloomer' like a mistake; they are CU and a flower. Hibs is Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibiscus is a flowering shrub, so it blooms, making it a bloomer.

clue.text: Teacher is hoping to embrace nurse

indicators.note: to embrace says the answer lies held within the following words

explanation.surface: A teacher hopes to hug a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: teaCHER IS Hoping. 'nurse' looks like a person but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope is to cherish it, holding it fondly.

clue.text: The antibodies destroyed illicit lover

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Antibodies have been wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' signals an anagram of THE ANTIBODIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is a colloquial term for a secret lover outside one's relationship.

clue.text: Relish old dance

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour, a relish

explanation.surface: Enjoy a dance from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb; it is a noun meaning flavour, TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Create agitation in prison

explanation.definitionFit: Stirring causes trouble, and stir is old slang for jail.

clue.text: Devious Roman made notes

indicators.note: devious, meaning winding, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crafty Roman wrote things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' signals an anagram of ROMAN MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the plural of memorandum, a written note.

clue.text: I spot one to be taken in — him?

definitions.text: I spot one to be taken in — him?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be taken in means the numeral for one goes inside the spot word

parts.note: a dot is a spot
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gullible victim who can be easily fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: I + DOT with I inside. The whole clue also defines: the one who is taken in is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a fool, the sort of person easily taken in by a con.

clue.text: Maybe use O2 arena

definitions.meaning: O2 is a mobile phone network, so using it might mean calling someone
an arena, as for boxing or the circus

explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to phone, perhaps on the O2 network, and a ring is an arena.

clue.text: Western character to cringe in fear receiving blow

indicators.note: receiving means the cringing word takes the blow inside it

parts.note: to cower is to cringe in fear
a punch is a blow

explanation.surface: A figure in a cowboy film flinches when hit.
explanation.walkthrough: COWER takes in PUNCH. 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpuncher is a cowboy, a stock figure of Westerns.
